entries.title: Letreros honoríficos recuerdan las vidas de dos puertorriqueños y los Disturbios de Humboldt Park
entries.summary: <p>Las comunidades de Humboldt Park y puertorriqueña se reunieron el jueves por la tarde para develar letreros de calle en honor a Rafael Cruz y Julio Osorio, dos hombres puertorriqueños cuya muerte en 1977 se convirtió en un catalizador para el cambio.</p><p>A Cruz y a Osorio les disparó y asesinó un policía de Chicago en junio de 1977 durante la violencia que estalló en Humboldt Park tras el Desfile del Día Puertorriqueño. La policía culpó a las pandillas; algunos en la comunidad acusaron a los oficiales de asaltar el parque y de golpear a quienes estaban haciendo un pícnic. Esto se conoce como los Disturbios de Humboldt Park o Humboldt Park Riots en inglés.</p><p>Las trágicas muertes de los dos hombres en un día que comenzó como una celebración de la herencia puertorriqueña alimentaron las demandas de justicia y desencadenaron décadas de activismo en el vecindario y en la comunidad puertorriqueña.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-cd0000" name="module-cd0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Un documental que cuenta la historia de los disturbios se estrenará el viernes durante el 45.º Festival Anual Puertorriqueño en Humboldt Park.</p><p>Para Roberto Cruz, el hermano de Rafael Cruz, la ceremonia de dedicación de la calle marcó el reconocimiento de una tragedia que cambió a su familia y ayudó a dar forma a la comunidad que lo rodea.</p><p>"La comunidad vino y ayudó a mi madre, la animó y me ayudó a llevarla de regreso a casa", dijo Cruz al reflexionar sobre el día en que asesinaron a su hermano. "Fue un día que cambió mi vida para siempre. Mi sangre literalmente fluye por este parque. Crecí en este parque. Sufrí en este parque".</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-107d33" name="image-107d33"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a9577cf/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/fb12f3a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b48ba12/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Roberto Cruz, hermano de Rafael Cruz, sostiene un letrero con el nombre de su hermano el jueves. Una porción de la Avenida California sobre la Avenida Evergreen, junto al Parque Humboldt, fue nombrada en honor a Rafael Cruz y Julio Osorio, a quienes les disparó y asesinó un policía de Chicago en junio de 1977 durante lo que se conoció como los disturbios de Humboldt Park." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b48ba12/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9ca2272/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b48ba12/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F16%2Fef%2Ff5eb2b384280893e0b7d3e6b6acd%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-24.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Roberto Cruz, hermano de Rafael Cruz, sostiene un letrero con el nombre de su hermano el jueves. Una porción de la Avenida California sobre la Avenida Evergreen, junto al Parque Humboldt, fue nombrada en honor a Rafael Cruz y Julio Osorio, a quienes les disparó y asesinó un policía de Chicago en junio de 1977 durante lo que se conoció como los disturbios de Humboldt Park.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>La dedicación de la calle coincidió con el primer de los cuatro días del festival anual, una de las celebraciones más grandes de la cultura puertorriqueña en la ciudad.</p><p>"Hoy no se trata solo de develar letreros de calle", dijo la concejal Jessie Fuentes (26.º). "Hoy se trata de asegurarnos de que no se borre nuestra historia".</p><p>Javier Vargas, cineasta que ha pasado la última década documentando la verdadera historia detrás de los incidentes y que ayudó a impulsar la nomenclatura de la calle, dijo que los letreros asegurarán que la historia de Cruz y Osorio nunca sea olvidada.</p><p>"La gente lo verá y podrá investigar y descubrir por qué sucedieron los disturbios", contó Vargas. "Es un símbolo de algo que ocurrió y permanecerá allí y no será olvidado".</p><p>Vargas comentó que las historias sobre los conflictos fueron una presencia constante durante su infancia, pero le preocupa que los nuevos residentes no estén familiarizados con esa historia a medida que Humboldt Park continúa cambiando.</p><p>"Cuando crecía, la gente siempre hablaba de estos disturbios y de cómo muchos cambios se debieron a ellos", dijo Vargas. "Ahora, la comunidad está más gentrificada y la gente ha olvidado lo que sucedió aquí en Humboldt Park".</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-7d9e5a" name="image-7d9e5a"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b413d66/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8d4983b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/077d8fc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Se han colocado nuevos letreros que muestran una designación honoraria para una parte de California Avenue junto a Humboldt Park. Los letreros que rinden homenaje a Julio Osorio y Rafael Cruz fueron develados el jueves." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/077d8fc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/feeaab3/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/077d8fc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F14%2F82%2F1c9175924439a9b1b3a58d96d19c%2Fstreetrenaminghumboldt-260612-17.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Se han colocado nuevos letreros que muestran una designación honoraria para una parte de California Avenue junto a Humboldt Park. Los letreros que rinden homenaje a Julio Osorio y Rafael Cruz fueron develados el jueves.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>José López, líder comunitario de muchos años, conectó la dedicación con los orígenes de una de las tradiciones más reconocibles de la comunidad.</p><p>"Un año después de este incidente, este asesinato violento, comenzamos nuestro desfile", dijo López. "Fue a raíz de este incidente que comenzamos el Desfile del Día del Pueblo Puertorriqueño".</p><p>Ese desfile ahora atrae a asistentes de toda la ciudad que vienen a celebrar la identidad, la resiliencia y la cultura puertorriqueñas.</p><p>Mientras las familias celebraban la develación de los letreros de calle honorarios, los líderes dijeron que la dedicación se trataba, ultimadamente, de asegurar que las historias de Rafael Cruz, Julio Osorio y de la comunidad puertorriqueña en general permanezcan visibles para las generaciones futuras.</p><p>En 1981, la Ciudad de Chicago llegó a un acuerdo con las familias de ambos hombres. El teniente del Departamento de Policía de Chicago (CPD), Thomas Walton, declaró inicialmente que le disparó a Osorio porque pensaba que tenía un arma. Una investigación posterior reveló que Osorio estaba desarmado; se encontró un cepillo negro cerca de él. Cruz fue alcanzado por una de las balas disparadas contra Osorio.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: ‘Ferris Bueller’s Day Off’ still makes Chicagoans proud, 40 years later
entries.summary: <p>Forty years ago this month, “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off” immortalized Chicago when the fictional teen skipped school and spent the day in the city with his girlfriend and best friend.</p><p>Their adventures showcased iconic sites such as the Art Institute of Chicago, the Flamingo sculpture in the Loop and the Willis Tower — or Sears Tower, as it was known in 1986.</p><p>TV and movie tour company On Location Tours held a Downtown walking tour tracing the steps of Ferris and friends on Thursday to mark the film’s release date. On Location also offers Downtown and suburban Chicago tours highlighting <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/01/21/from-the-fugitive-to-the-dark-knight-whats-the-best-movie-filmed-in-chicago" target="_blank" >films</a> such as “The Blues Brothers,” “The Fugitive,” “The Breakfast Club” and “High Fidelity”.</p><p>But its "Ferris" tour particularly resonates with locals, said Dan Goldenrose, who leads On Location’s Chicago tours.</p><p>“Chicagoans feel a sense of pride. In those days, not a lot was filmed here. It was a novelty,” he said.</p><p>The film’s director, John Hughes, grew up in Northbrook and called the movie his “love letter” to Chicago, Goldenrose said. In the film, “he used the city as a character.”</p><p>Goldenrose is also an actor who has appeared in “The Bear,” “Shameless,” “Chicago PD” and other productions. The Morton Grove native recalled taking the Skokie Swift, also known as the Yellow Line, to Wrigley Field when he was 12, so he especially loves the baseball scenes in "Ferris."</p><p>Ben Stumpe was one of more than 30 people who joined Thursday’s tour. "Ferris" is his mother’s favorite movie, and he also fell in love with it at age 9. Stumpe grew up in Missouri, and the film inspired him to move to Chicago and attend DePaul University.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-270000" name="image-270000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a8fef6d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F1e%2Fb2%2F49cf83cb48fc8ed90a75361f1f88%2Fferris-260615-28.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/716125a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F1e%2Fb2%2F49cf83cb48fc8ed90a75361f1f88%2Fferris-260615-28.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/30f27e8/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F1e%2Fb2%2F49cf83cb48fc8ed90a75361f1f88%2Fferris-260615-28.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Ben Stumpe and Meghan Callaghan joined the "Ferris Bueller’s Day Off " walking tour. entries.title: 4 charged in connection with attempted robbery of undercover ATF agents in Country Club Hills
entries.summary: <p>Four people are charged in connection with an attempted robbery of undercover federal agents Tuesday in Country Club Hills that resulted in two suspects being shot by officers.</p><p>Undercover agents with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives were investigating a firearm-trafficking operation around 5:30 p.m. in the 18800 block of Loretto Lane, where they had arranged to buy firearms as part of the investigation, according to federal court documents.</p><p>Amir Fagan, 19, Demond Edwards, 18, and a third person arrived in a car, got out and pointed firearms at the undercover agents, trying to rob them, according to the U.S. attorney’s office for Northern Illinois.</p><p>Another group of ATF agents arrived at the scene, and one of them fired shots, striking Fagan, prosecutors said.</p><p>The driver of the suspects’ car, Chashonn Toney, 18, rammed his car into an ATF vehicle while trying to flee the scene, prosecutors said.</p><p>Edwards ran from the scene, but an undercover Chicago police officer chased him and stopped him about two blocks away, according to prosecutors and Chicago’s police oversight agency. Edwards struck the officer “multiple times” in the face and body, leading the officer to shoot Edwards, prosecutors said.</p><p>Both suspects who were shot were in critical condition and were taken to hospitals, where their conditions were stabilized — and where they also were placed under arrest. A law enforcement officer was taken to a hospital for observation as well.</p><p>Three other people were apprehended at the scene, officials said.</p><p>But four people were named in the criminal complaint filed Thursday in federal court: Fagan, Edwards, Toney and Tevin Curlee, 29.</p><p>Fagan, of Harvey, and Edwards, of Markham, are both charged with attempted robbery. Toney, of Robbins, is charged with forcibly assaulting a law enforcement officer. Curlee, of Country Club Hills, is charged with unlawfully possessing and transferring a machine gun. Curlee is accused of selling a handgun equipped with a machine gun conversion device to undercover officers June 3 in south suburban Crestwood.</p><p>Each of their first appearances in court are pending.</p><p>The federal investigation into the incident is ongoing.</p>

entries.title: Review: Mumford & Sons weathers storm to bring Prizefighter Tour to Wrigley Field
entries.summary: <p>“Ladies and gentleman, we are live for the main event!” It was the message tens of thousands of fans had been waiting hours for Thursday night as the stage lights and video screens turned on at Wrigley Field at 10:43 p.m. After persistent delays from the severe weather that rocked the Chicago area, Mumford & Sons finally brought its Prizefighter Tour to life at the ballpark, though questions lingered if it was a total knockout victory against Mother Nature or one bad call to let the show go on at all.</p><p>Wrigley Field has batted a thousand with its concert schedule over the last 21 years, never canceling a show outright due to weather, even though long delays and adjusted set times have been commonplace for previous dates with Pearl Jam, Chris Stapleton and Billy Joel. Rain or shine is a typical policy for the industry but cases of extreme weather typically usurp that standard. When doors opened at 8:30 p.m. on Thursday night, Cook County was under a tornado warning, which was issued after 8 p.m. and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/06/12/chicago-severe-weather-tornadoes-power-outage-comed-customers-englewood" target="_blank" ><u>expired less than an hour later</u></a>. A severe thunderstorm warning was in effect until 9 p.m. Lightning crackled in the sky as fans finally entered the Friendly Confines.</p><p>Throughout the day, many ticketholders had aired disapproval on social media for organizers’ decisions and the lack of consistent and timely communication. The first official update came in at 2:30 p.m. with Wrigley Field and the band informing fans they were monitoring weather patterns and that gates were still scheduled to open at 5 p.m. Less than a half-hour before that scheduled time, the band posted that the opening of gates was pushed to 8:30 p.m. with Mumford & Sons taking the stage at 10 p.m. and the opening acts, Caamp and Dylan Gossett, sacrificed due to the adjusted timeframe.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li Many fans online called for organizers to postpone the show and reschedule, citing how Jimmy Eat World and Northerly Island had done so hours prior.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Due to the timing of notifications, a number of fans had already made the trek to Wrigleyville and were left stranded as the height of the severe weather moved in, leading to numerous comments for organizers to postpone the show and reschedule, citing how Jimmy Eat World and Northerly Island had done so hours prior.</p><p>Also at issue was that Wrigley Field traditionally has a strict 11 p.m. curfew for night events, though the band played until about 12:30 a.m. with <a class="Link" href="https://www.reddit.com/r/mumfordandsons/comments/1u349zk/wrigley/" target="_blank" >neighbors voicing concerns over noise levels</a>, including a large series of fireworks that went off when Mumford & Sons opened with “Begin Again,” nearly 45 minutes after the newly updated set time. Organizers face a minimum $45,000 fine, according to the 44th Ward office.</p><p>Wrigley Field declined to comment, deferring to Live Nation.</p><p>“The safety of fans, artists, staff and crew is always our top priority. Weather conditions were monitored closely with updates provided as information became available. The event proceeded only after venue management, city officials and weather experts determined it was safe to do so,” Live Nation said in a statement. The statement did not elaborate on whether Mumford & Sons would incur the hefty fine written into the bylaws of the neighborhood noise ordinance.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/24f0f25/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe3%2Fc1%2F8c5707b345b89d54d43469185d88%2Fmumfordsons-260613-23.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ff1e920/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe3%2Fc1%2F8c5707b345b89d54d43469185d88%2Fmumfordsons-260613-23.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/24f0f25/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe3%2Fc1%2F8c5707b345b89d54d43469185d88%2Fmumfordsons-260613-23.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>This has been the show we’ve been looking forward to pretty much the most out of all this tour. And we’re so happy to be here with you,” Marcus Mumford told the crowd Thursday after storms delayed the band’s performance. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The band largely stuck to its bread-and-butter folk songbook, with some numbers like the “Prizefighter” title track and “Badlands” way too slow and drawn out for this late-night hour. But the energy quickly picked up with the Southern rock swagger of “Truth,” accompanied by a swath of fireballs and the near hoedown of “The Cave.” For the anthemic rocker “Ditmas,” Mumford used it as a chance to embark on a spirited run through the ballpark much to fans’ delight. Later, Lovett shouted out to those in the rafters as a “reminder of what it’s like to be the person in the back of the room.”</p><p>Mumford & Sons also graciously gave space for the canceled openers too, inviting Dylan Gossett for a duet on “Here” (originally featuring Chris Stapleton on the recorded track) and covering Caamp’s “All The Debts I Owe” with singer Taylor Meier. That song, along with “Timshel” and “Reminder,” were performed at a small B stage near the first baseline as the core three members of Mumford & Sons quietly huddled up with a sole acoustic guitar and were successful in their mission to “get 50,000 Chicagoans to shut the f--- up at the same time” to hear the tender melodies.</p><p>By the time the band returned to the main stage for a solid closer of hits “Rushmere” and “I Will Wait,” Mumford was decked out in his own personalized Cubs jersey to remember the night as the rest of us would, for better or worse. “Chicago always sticks with us, we f------ love you, we f------ love our crew, we love the people in this building,” he said. “We’re so grateful to you.”</p><p><i>Contributing: Elijah James</i></p><hr><p><b></b></p><h3>Mumford & Sons set list for June 11, 2026, show at Wrigley Field</h3><p>Begin Again<br>Babel<br>Little Lion Man<br>White Blank Page<br>Awake My Soul<br>Lover of the Light<br>Hopeless Wanderer<br>Prizefighter<br>Badlands<br>Believe<br>Truth<br>Ditmas<br>The Cave<br>Here (with Dylan Gossett)<br>Rubber Band Man<br>Delta<br>The Wolf<br>Timshel<br>Reminder<br>All the Debts I Owe (Caamp cover, with Caamp’s Taylor Meier)<br>Rushmere<br>The Banjo SongI<br> Will Wait<br>Conversation with My Son (Gangsters and Angels)</p>

entries.title: Las facturas de impuestos sobre la propiedad de Cook County se retrasan nuevamente: esta vez por 2 meses
entries.summary: <p>Las facturas de impuestos sobre la propiedad, que generalmente se envían en julio, se retrasarán una vez más, según la presidenta de la Junta del Condado de Cook, Toni Preckwinkle.</p><p>Preckwinkle, quien anunció el retraso de dos meses el martes, dijo que tiene la intención de reabrir un programa de préstamos sin intereses para los organismos gubernamentales que dependen de los ingresos de impuestos a la propiedad que ahora no recibirán a tiempo.</p><p>Los distritos fiscales suburbanos, como escuelas y bibliotecas, que de otro modo tendrían que recurrir a costosos préstamos a corto plazo para cubrir sus presupuestos, pueden en su lugar pedir prestado del Programa del Fondo Puente para Impuestos a la Propiedad de $300 millones del condado, dijo Preckwinkle.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-9a0000" name="module-9a0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Ese programa se asemeja a uno establecido el año pasado, cuando las facturas de impuestos se <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/11/07/cook-county-property-tax-bills-due-dec-15-after-several-months-delay" target="_blank" >retrasaron cuatro meses</a> debido a un problema de computación.</p><p>Sin embargo, las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS) no serían elegibles para ese programa de préstamos. Eso podría ser un problema para CPS, que el año pasado pagó <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/education/2025/12/19/property-tax-payment-delay-costs-chicago-public-schools-almost-a-quarter-million-dollars-a-day" target="_blank" >$220,000 en intereses por día en préstamos a corto plazo</a> que tomó para cumplir con la nómina.</p><p>Los funcionarios de CPS dijeron que el retraso en la factura de impuestos del año pasado los ha obligado a obtener al menos $1.6 mil millones en préstamos a corto plazo para gastos operativos y otro préstamo de $246 millones para mantener solvente el fondo de pensiones de sus maestros, lo que generará $33 millones en pagos de intereses en el futuro.</p><p>CPS no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.</p><p>El programa de préstamos es necesario, dijo Preckwinkle, porque los retrasos en el pago de las facturas de impuestos pueden costar a distintos organismos enormes cantidades de dinero, especialmente cuando toman préstamos a corto plazo. Preckwinkle mencionó que se darán más detalles el próximo mes, cuando anticipa que la Junta del Condado de Cook aprobará la medida.</p><p>“Estamos anunciando esto ahora porque los gobiernos locales necesitan tiempo para planificar”, dijo Preckwinkle en un comunicado. “Este fondo transitorio brinda a las escuelas, bibliotecas, parques, distritos de bomberos y otros gobiernos locales una herramienta a corto plazo para continuar sirviendo a los residentes mientras seguimos con el trabajo más profundo de arreglar un sistema de impuestos a la propiedad fragmentado”, aseguró.</p><p>Preckwinkle destacó el retraso como una mayor necesidad de reforma de impuestos en un año que ha visto algunas modificaciones a las leyes fiscales, incluyendo cambios legislativos <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/05/31/illinois-lawmakers-legislation-homeowners-equity-property-taxes-debt-tax-foreclosure" target="_blank" >en las ventas de impuestos a la propiedad</a>.</p><p>Pero el retraso del año pasado fue sólo la punta del iceberg.</p><p>En los últimos 30 años, la recaudación de los impuestos a la propiedad ha superado la inflación y crecido “<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/03/30/property-taxes-cook-county-treasurer-study" target="_blank" >muy por encima del crecimiento de los salarios</a>”, según un <a class="Link" href="https://www.cookcountytreasurer.com/skyrocketingpropertytaxes.aspx" target="_blank" >informe</a> reciente de la oficina de la tesorera del Condado de Cook. La recaudación del impuesto a la propiedad del condado aumentó de $6.8 mil millones en 1995 a $19.2 mil millones en 2024. Eso son $10 mil millones más de lo que habría sido si simplemente hubiera mantenido el ritmo de la inflación.</p><p>Las escuelas a nivel de condado, que representan aproximadamente la mitad de la factura total de impuestos, también han visto las demandas de impuestos dispararse un 189%, o $6.9 mil millones.</p><p>Algunos, incluido el extasador del Condado de Cook, James Houlihan, han solicitado una revisión del sistema a gran escala. Ha sugerido desvincular a las escuelas públicas del método actual de financiamiento, en el que dependen únicamente de los ingresos provenientes de los impuestos a la propiedad.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: White Sox slugger Munetaka Murakami is running — slowly — two weeks since straining hamstring
entries.summary: <p>Munetaka Murakami is running … slowly. OK, more like jogging. And not for very long.</p><p>However you describe it, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a>’ home-run leader was in motion in short left field before the game Friday against the Dodgers, two weeks to the day since straining his right hamstring while running to first base.</p><p>Under the watchful eyes of Sox trainers — and almost a dozen Japanese reporters — Murakami ran for the second consecutive day, but he said his recovery remains within the initial timeline of four to six weeks.</p><p>“There’s progress, obviously,” manager Will Venable said. “He’s got the hammy, so he wasn’t out there sprinting at full speed. But I think everyone’s encouraged with the progress, and [he was] back out there today.</p><p>“There’s a lot of boxes he’s got to check still as you look at the progression between the running and the hitting and how the recovery is going. No updated timeline.”</p><p>“It’s coming along really well, progressing day by day,” Murakami said through interpreter Kenzo Yagi. “I think I’m doing well on the rehab itself. The pain has obviously gone down after two weeks. I’m really feeling good. I’m just going to keep focusing on what I have in front of me and stay very patient with myself.”</p><p>Patience will be key. The last thing the Sox want is for Murakami to aggravate the injury while rehabbing it or return to early and potentially do worse damage. Even though the first baseman has missed 10 games, he still leads the Sox — and entered Friday tied for third in the majors with the Twins’ Byron Buxton — with 20 home runs.</p><p>Murakami realizes he’s missing out on valuable experience learning the major leagues. He’ll spend game time supporting his teammates in any way he can.</p><p>“Playing is where you get the most experience, obviously,” he said. “But I’m just trying to do whatever’s possible [on] the bench, try to visualize stuff so that when I get back out there, I’m able to contribute the best I can.”</p><p>The Sox haven’t missed him to the point that they’re desperate to get him back. They were 6-4 without him, and they beat the major-league-leading Braves twice this week, with and without the long ball. Miguel Vargas and Braden Montgomery homered in a 6-5 win — Montgomery’s coming in walk-off fashion — and the Sox played small ball to win 2-1.</p><p>Still, imagine this new-look Sox lineup with Murakami in it. Since his injury, the team has called up Jacob Gonzalez and Braden Montgomery from Triple-A Charlotte. Gonzalez, who hit 19 homers in 52 games at Charlotte this season, was 8-for-26 with a homer since being promoted, and Montgomery was 4-for-9 with two doubles and a homer.</p><p>General manager Chris Getz will have to figure out who goes when Murakami returns, but if both rookies stay, the Sox’ lineup lengthens with potential pop. Vargas and Colson Montgomery are tied for second on the team with 16 homers, and Randall Grichuk quickly could join them. He has six homers in only 27 games, playing mostly against left-handed pitching.</p><p>It’s too bad both Murakami and Dodgers two-way star Shohei Ohtani were out of the lineup. Ohtani didn’t start because of inflammation in his left knee. The Dodgers didn’t put him on the injured list, and they hope he’s able to play Saturday. Murakami said the two remain close after playing on Team Japan in the World Baseball Classic.</p><p>It probably also was a bummer for Murakami’s parents, who made the trip from Japan but won’t get to see their son play.</p><p>“I’m really happy that they’re here,” Murakami said. “Obviously, I wanted to play in front of them, but that’s for next time. I just want to heal up quickly, and maybe next time they can see me play.”</p><p>Sox fans are counting the days.</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" entries.title: Pritzker can't expect to escape Bears stadium bill blame
entries.summary: <p>Gov. JB Pritzker last week squarely placed the responsibility for passing a Bears stadium bill on the team itself, and had some unsolicited lobbying advice for the Bears as he attempted to brush off his own session attendance issues.</p><p>The governor continued to downplay his own role in passing a stadium or stadium-related bill, saying it was Bears management which “decided to glom on to the megaprojects bill that I proposed.”</p><p>Um, he didn’t exactly resist that move, and the Bears’ addition became the most highlighted part of the bill, to the point where lots of members believed Pritzker was using the Bears to pass an idea that had long ago hit a brick wall in both legislative chambers.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-110000" name="module-110000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Columnists bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Columnists</h2><br><i>In-depth political coverage, sports analysis, entertainment reviews and cultural commentary.</i><br></div> </div><p>Pritzker also said he’d be “happy” to call a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/06/09/pritzker-bears-stadium-indiana-illinois-special-session-arlington-heights" >special session</a>, but only if the Bears “figure out how they can get the Legislature, both sides around the same bill.”</p><p>And then he offered some belated statehouse lobbying advice: “You’ve got to work the hallways, as you know, in a very, very busy session,” Pritzker told reporters after accurately saying the Bears made “some fumbles” the past few years. “You've got to really talk to every legislator if you want to get something done,” he said.</p><p>Pritzker said he’s received calls from the Bears since session ended, but didn’t say if he repeated that same advice.</p><p>My associate Isabel Miller pointed out to the governor that he had repeatedly urged the General Assembly to move more quickly on the megaprojects bill: “Looking back, do you think spending more time in Springfield working out issues might have produced a different outcome?” </p><p>As I told my newsletter subscribers on June 8, Pritzker was in Springfield for just 22 session days this spring.</p><p>“I spent a lot of time in Springfield,” the governor insisted, adding, “I'm not a legislator,” and said he has “a whole lot of responsibilities that aren't legislative.”</p><p>According to his legislative calendar, Pritzker was in Springfield two days in January and two days in February, four days in March and three days in April. During the crucial final session month of May, the governor was in town 11 out of 19 session days.</p><p>The governor’s calendar also shows that he had just 14 scheduled in-person meetings with individual rank-and-file legislators in Springfield during all of spring session, including only one meeting on his calendar to talk about the Bears stadium with top negotiators Sen. Bill Cunningham, D-Chicago, and Rep. Kam Buckner, D-Chicago, the day before session was scheduled to adjourn.</p><p>One top Pritzker insider explained that the governor often takes impromptu calls from members to talk about their projects and/or their bills, which wouldn’t be on the official schedule.</p><p>The insider also pointed to how the disjointed, deliberately uncoordinated legislative calendar made it difficult to schedule events at the executive mansion because the two chambers were so rarely in town together until May. He hosted four such events this year (Women Wear Pink, the Black Caucus, Latino Caucus and Asian American Caucus).</p><p>Pritzker has been sharply criticized for quite a while for focusing more on the national political front than on governing Illinois. And while all or parts of several bills on his priority list did pass, the danger for Pritzker is that this Bears failure will overshadow everything else and highlight his national ambitions because it’s something that transcends the statehouse. His attendance record, while not a complete look at his work, does him no favors.</p><p>Isabel also asked the governor last week if, going forward, he was “planning to be more present in Springfield.”</p><p>“I'm in Springfield a lot,” Pritzker replied, saying he often invites legislators to his appearances in their districts. However, his calendar shows he attended events outside Springfield on 18 different session days, which would make it difficult for legislators to attend.</p><p>Pritzker also said he called “several” Republican legislators “during the final portions of the session to make sure that they were on board” with the Bears bill. He did not say if he phoned any Democrats.</p><p>I’ve said this before and I’ll say it again: The governor has a very good executive staff, if too overburdened. But there’s no substitute for a present governor. Legislators are generally a needy bunch. They see him on national TV during session and wonder why he isn’t attending to them. That’s simple statehouse reality and has been forever.</p><p>Pritzker was right when he told reporters, "You've got to really talk to every legislator if you want to get something done." He might think about that advice during upcoming sessions.</p><p><i>Rich Miller also publishes Capitol Fax, a daily political newsletter, and CapitolFax.com.</i></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-370000" name="module-370000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody">Send letters to <a class="Link" href="mailto:letters@suntimes.com" target="_blank" >letters@suntimes.com</a>. More about <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/submitting-opinion-and-letters" >how to submit here</a>.</div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Medical group leader apologizes to Northwestern researcher, others booted from conference over Trump critique
entries.summary: <p>The head of the American Diabetes Association has issued a public apology to a Northwestern researcher and other diabetes experts who were escorted out of the group’s conference while distributing an editorial critical of President Donald Trump’s administration.</p><p>“I am deeply sorry for the hurt, frustration and the pain that resulted,” Charles Henderson, the association’s CEO, said in a <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W7K2j3Rs-Qg" target="_blank" ><u>video posted on YouTube</u></a>. “Also [I] want to apologize to the broader diabetes community. Many members of our community were disturbed, disappointed and concerned by what occurred.”</p><p>Henderson went on to say the Virginia-based association would undergo an independent review of what happened last week at the New Orleans conference and will share steps the organization will take in the future.</p><p>The apology was made public Wednesday, days after Justin Ryder, a pediatric obesity specialist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and Lurie Children’s Hospital, returned to the Chicago area after he was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/06/08/northwestern-researcher-among-group-kicked-out-of-conference-for-distributing-paper-critical-of-trump" >escorted by private security and local police from the conference</a>. Officers confiscated his conference badge and he was told he would be arrested if he tried to return.</p><p>The incident happened June 5 while he and other researchers were distributing an editorial titled, “Misguided Brushes of a Pen Continue to Dismantle and Destroy Biomedical Research in the United States: We Can No Longer Afford Complacency and Fear. We Must All Act Now!” It had been published in a medical journal called Diabetes Care, published by the American Diabetes Association.</p><p>Ryder, who was not involved in writing the editorial, previously told the Sun-Times it was important for the scientific community to distribute knowledge and not be censored.</p><p>“It’s important to me for the word to get out there, that what’s going on in this country, to science, is not acceptable, and that it’s going to be damaging,” Ryder said. “People are going to lose their lives because we’re not going to be able to create new treatments or vaccines that can be really beneficial for human health.”</p><p>An online petition that had garnered more than 7,000 signatures called on the American Diabetes Association to apologize and make a commitment to a “policy of freedom of expression and scientific inquiry at all times.”</p><p>In his three-minute online apology, Henderson did not explicitly address concerns regarding the First Amendment, but he did say the organization was committed to science.</p><p>“The ADA will continue to advocate for robust NIH funding, support the pursuit of scientific discovery, and advocate for the broader research community whose work advances knowledge, drives innovation and ultimately improves the lives of people living with diabetes, obesity and related conditions,” Henderson said in the video.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/06/08/northwestern-researcher-among-group-kicked-out-of-conference-for-distributing-paper-critical-of-trump" >Northwestern researcher among group kicked out of conference for distributing paper critical of Trump</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: 'Is Mr. Boutros here?' Judge drops fraud charges, calls out U.S. attorney as ‘Broadview 6’ fallout grows
entries.summary: <p>A judge granted the feds' request Friday to drop charges against two defendants in a massive COVID-19 testing fraud scheme handled by the same prosecutor as the tainted “Broadview Six” case.</p><p>The dismissal marked the first case to crumble under what another judge called a “credibility crisis” swirling around U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros’ office following the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/broadview-ice-protest-grand-jury-transcript-kat-abughazaleh-trump" target="_blank" >collapse of the Broadview prosecution</a> last month.</p><p>On Thursday, the feds <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/11/broadview-six-grand-jury-misconduct-federal-prosecutors-drop-charges-loretto-hospital-covid-fraud" target="_blank" >moved to drop charges</a> against two “low level of operators” linked to former Loretto Hospital chief financial officer Anosh Ahmed. They did so to avoid a hearing that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/10/hearing-in-loretto-hospital-case-could-address-claims-of-prosecutors-misconduct-if-feds-dont-drop-it" target="_blank" >could have put Boutros on the witness stand</a> to address fresh allegations of prosecutorial misconduct. </p><p>“We have cases throughout this building that are all in turmoil,” U.S. District Judge Sharon Johnson Coleman said while dismissing the charges Friday. “Pandora’s Box has been opened … I don’t know if by doing this you get to put everything back in the box”</p><p>It’s been three weeks since Boutros announced the permanent dismissal of charges against the remaining defendants in the prosecution of the “Broadview Six,” originally a felony conspiracy case filed last fall against a group of Operation Midway Blitz protesters.</p><p>The case was later pared down<b> </b>to a misdemeanor matter against four of those protestors. Then Boutros dropped the case entirely after U.S. District Judge April Perry discovered apparent misconduct by Assistant U.S. Attorney Sheri Mecklenburg during grand jury proceedings.</p><div Midway Blitz was dropped during a hearing at the Dirksen Federal Courthouse. They were the last four members of the so-called “Broadview Six” to face criminal charges.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Ashlee Rezin/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The alleged misconduct included Mecklenburg improperly putting her credibility on the line to support criminal charges, wrongly dismissing grand jurors from the proceedings, and having conversations with grand jurors outside the grand jury room.</p><p>Transcripts of the typically secret grand jury proceedings were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/06/09/broadview-six-grand-jury-midway-blitz-boutros-trump" target="_blank" >released earlier this week</a>, showing Mecklenburg acknowledged having improper discussions with grand jurors.</p><p>Mecklenburg was also handling the Loretto investigation, which Coleman argued was just “as serious” as the case before Perry — though it did not prompt an appearance from Boutros himself on Friday. Coleman made her frustrations clear before permanently dismissing charges against Mahmood Sami Khan and Suhaib Ahmad Chaudhry.</p><p>“Is Mr. Boutros here?” Coleman asked. “This is serious.”</p><p>Coleman also addressed what she assumed was a “level of angst” within Boutros' office, as other prosecutors were sent to answer for alleged misconduct on his behalf.</p><p>“It's not a one-man show,” Coleman said. “[And] If there is a one-man show … it’s the U.S. attorney. He decides … That’s why he’s got the big job. But he’s not here.”</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2025/06/17/former-loretto-hospital-executive-charged-fake-covid-testing-scheme" target="_blank" >The fraud case</a> involving Khan and Chaudhry “arises out of a single, widespread scheme to submit more than $800 million in false claims” to the federal government “for reimbursement of COVID-19 testing of uninsured individuals,” Mecklenburg wrote earlier this year.</p><p>The scheme lasted from June 2021 through March 2022, “when the government program ran out of money,” she added.</p><p>The false claims resulted in payouts totaling $293 million, according to the indictment.</p><p>Just days after the Broadview Six dismissal, defense attorneys for Khan and Chaudhry accused Mecklenburg of similar misconduct. “Grand juries are meant to protect the innocent — like Sami Khan,” his attorneys said Friday.</p><p>“But, in this case the system broke and he was charged. Without individuals, lawyers and judges who challenge the government, abuse of the system would go undetected,” they wrote. “Sami thanks the Broadview 6 lawyers and the judges across cases who had the courage to demand the system operate with integrity. The system broke — but ultimately, it worked.”</p><p>Prosecutors will continue their case against Ahmed, who remains in Serbia fighting extradition. His attorney also sought dismissal Friday, but Coleman denied the request because he hasn't been arraigned.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/broadview-ice-protest-grand-jury-transcript-kat-abughazaleh-trump" target="_blank" >‘Broadview Six’ charges dropped as Chicago’s top federal prosecutor admits case was tainted by misconduct</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/06/09/broadview-six-grand-jury-midway-blitz-boutros-trump" target="_blank" >Transcripts reveal tension, improprieties during ‘Broadview 6’ grand jury hearings</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/06/08/broadview-six-andrew-boutros-federal-prosecutor-justice-department-doj" target="_blank" >Over 100 ex-federal prosecutors call out ‘failure of leadership’ by Chicago’s embattled U.S. attorney</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
